name: xAI

profile.reading: This is the original building of xAI's Colossus supercomputer campus in South Memphis, at 3231 Riverport Road. The site is a former Electrolux appliance factory (785,000 square feet), purchased by Phoenix Investors in December 2023 for $35 million; its existing shell and proximity to wastewater treatment infrastructure and the Mississippi River let xAI complete construction in roughly 122 days, versus an industry-standard multi-year timeline, with Dell Technologies and Supermicro handling infrastructure and Nvidia supplying GPU hardware. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, finalized its decision to build in Memphis in March 2024, announced the project publicly in June 2024, began operations in July 2024, and officially launched Colossus with 100,000 GPUs in September 2024, primarily to train xAI's Grok chatbot while also supporting X (formerly Twitter) and SpaceX workloads. By June 2025 the GPU count had grown to roughly 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 units, with power consumption rising from about 150 MW at launch to a 250 MW maximum, an amount well beyond the facility's original 150 MW grid connection, so xAI has supplemented it with 35 gas turbines (422 MW combined capacity) and 168 Tesla Megapack batteries. That gas-turbine buildout drew significant environmental scrutiny: the Southern Environmental Law Center has characterized the facility as likely the largest industrial emitter of nitrogen oxides in Memphis, citing an estimated 1,200 to 2,000 tons of NOx annually, and xAI initially operated the turbines without permits under a Shelby County regulatory loophole covering only generators on-site 365-plus days, before EPA standards revised in January 2026 required permits for large temporary methane turbines. Water usage (an expected 5 million-plus gallons daily) and local arsenic-contamination concerns prompted an approved $80 million wastewater recycling facility. No formal public review process preceded the project's announcement, and Memphis residents have reported chronic respiratory issues and learned of the facility primarily from local news coverage rather than a community process.

profile.reading: This is xAI's Colossus 2 expansion building, at 5400 Tulane Road in the Whitehaven area of Memphis, part of the company's Colossus supercomputer campus alongside the original Colossus 1 building at 3231 Riverport Road, tracked separately elsewhere in this registry. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, purchased this roughly 1-million-square-foot Whitehaven property in March 2025 for about $80 million, a project reported to add 320 jobs and to house additional GPU infrastructure, with an additional 110,000 GB200 GPUs planned for this second data center as of mid-2025 reporting, part of xAI's stated goal of expanding Colossus to 1 million GPUs total across the campus. The expansion is also intended to eventually let xAI operate its power supply independently from Memphis municipal utilities, following the Colossus 1 building's heavy reliance on supplemental gas turbines (35 units, 422 MW combined) and Tesla Megapack battery storage after its original 150 MW grid connection proved insufficient for GPU-cluster power demand, a buildout that drew scrutiny from the Southern Environmental Law Center over nitrogen oxide emissions and from residents over water usage and air quality. Colossus 1 launched in September 2024 with 100,000 GPUs and had grown to roughly 230,000 GPUs (a mix of H100, H200, and GB200 units) by June 2025, with total campus power consumption reported in the range of up to 250 MW at Colossus 1 alone and Memphis-area peak demand concerns cited around 3 GW; this entry does not apply Colossus 1's specific GPU or power figures to this separate Colossus 2 building. No building-specific square footage, MW capacity, or opening date for Colossus 2 itself was located in sourcing reachable this session beyond the roughly 1-million-square-foot property size and March 2025 acquisition date.

reading:
xAI, Elon Musk's AI company widely reported as founded in 2023, operates as a private company, not an SEC filer, with recent office leases in Palo Alto, California reported by real estate trade press in January 2026. The site's own copyright notice in 2026 reads SpaceXAI LLC, reflecting closer ties to Musk's other companies following xAI's 2025 merger with X, formerly Twitter, a corporate detail this entry notes without further investigating.

xAI's flagship facility, Colossus, sits at a former Electrolux manufacturing site in Memphis, Tennessee. The build decision was finalized in March 2024, announced publicly in June 2024, and went operational in September 2024 with 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs installed in 122 days. By December 2024 the system had doubled to 200,000 GPUs, pushing peak power draw from 150 to 250 megawatts, and by June 2025 the configuration had shifted to a mix of 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 GPUs, with another 110,000 GB200 GPUs planned for a second data center. xAI has stated an intent to eventually reach 1 million GPUs. The company expanded into Southaven, Mississippi in 2025 and purchased a 1 million square foot property in Whitehaven, Memphis in March 2025.

The registry here tracks 3 xAI facilities, all in Tennessee, consistent with the Memphis-area Colossus buildout. Colossus's documented 250 megawatt peak power draw at only 200,000 GPUs, reached within months of launch, is one of the fastest capacity ramps of any facility referenced in this registry's operator research so far, a concrete illustration of the compute-and-power scaling pressure this site's broader dataset tracks.
